spans.text: Yokai are the result of the eidomantic web twisting and knotting as tragedy vibrates through it - it’s a glitch in the system that produces life resembling the dark shadows in mortal hearts. False Eidolons are among the most dire of these shadows: when a great enough number of mortals feel spurned by the Eidolons, misunderstand their purpose, or worship a false version of them, that collective misunderstanding can cause a false Eidolon to appear that serves as the avatar for those dark misunderstandings.

The reason why only eidolic deities seem to generate false Eidolons is largely a mystery, but since yokai are the result of eidomantic radiation giving shape to new life through a glitch in the web, it is likely due to the fact that eidolic deities are more in tune with that radiation, so their conceptual “shape” is more easily achieved. Yokai resembling lesser gods have appeared, but are usually a form of daiyokai rather than a false Eidolon (though in common terms, false Eidolons are known to be called daiyokai).
Generally only one false Eidolon exists at a given time for each eidolic deity, but this isn’t a hard and fast rule. They only appear once every millenia, if at all.

False Eidolons know that they aren’t proper Eidolons in their heart, but they were born to fill the role an Eidolon “failed” to fill. Their existence is built around this lie, and they will do anything to fool the world - even themselves - into believing they are the true Eidolon. This obsession borders on insanity, and means they cannot accept that they aren’t who they say they are. They will serve as a dark mimic of their eidolic counterpart - taking actions they believe they would take, gathering their followers under their sway, and attempting to raise themselves to the social status of a god.

Furthermore, if they manage to build a following of at least 1000 worshippers in one community or are surrounded by at least 50 of their true followers, they can supernaturally influence the ability of others to detect them for what they are. Those with special senses that could detect yokai or discern divine power will mistake the false Eidolon for a god instead of a fiend, and will even detect the alignment they wish to be.

False Eidolons emulate the eidolic nature of their counterparts. Like most yokai, if their body is destroyed they will reform in the Realm of Shadow, but they take considerable amounts of time to do so compared to regular yokai. If killed by an eidolic artifact, or by eidolic damage from a being greater than themselves, they will be destroyed permanently. As usual, if destroyed in the Realm of Shadow they are also destroyed permanently.

A false Eidolon has the same portfolio and some sway over the same domains as the Eidolon they mirror, though they express them in unintentionally twisted ways. They know everything required to emulate the Eidolon, such as knowledge of the divine realm, aspects, and they can sense large-scale events that involve the Eidolon. Furthermore, if a creature within 100 miles of a false Eidolon offers a prayer to their corresponding Eidolon, the false Eidolon becomes aware of it and may intercept the Eidolon’s awareness of it entirely.

The false Eidolons have a special trait, “Siphon the Devout”, which effectively allows them to avoid death as long as they’re surrounded by worshippers. When running a false Eidolon it is important to treat this skill as a narrative hurdle: disillusioning their followers or forcing a false Eidolon to draw so liberally from their followers’ lives that it frightens them should be part of the experience of dealing with one. If unaddressed, this trait may leave them effectively immortal in some situations.
